aliases: Google Kansas City, Missouri data center
status_as_of_cutoff: site work-construction: KCMO Council approved Rocky Branch Creek data-center campus zoning/development-plan actions in 2022 and a roughly 500-acre major MPD amendment on 2024-03-07; Port KC authorized up to $10 billion in Project Mica taxable revenue bonds on 2025-07-28; Google's current data-center locations page lists Kansas City, Missouri in development; Google/local media reporting on 2026-02-12/2026-02-13 identified Project Mica as a Google campus with construction underway, and local visual reporting showed cranes on site. No building-level permit, inspection, CO, utility interconnection, energization, commissioning, or live-service record was located in this refresh.
evidence_grade: B: official KCMO/Port KC records establish land-use and financing actions plus current public project scope; Google official location page confirms Kansas City is in development; construction-start evidence is company/local-media/trade reporting, not a building-permit or energization record.

actions.result_status: Council passed Ordinance 220949 rezoning about 360 acres at the northeast corner of Highway 169 and I-435 to District MPD and approving a development plan/preliminary plat for a data center campus.
actions.access_caveat: Preliminary land-use/development-plan approval; not a building permit, certificate of occupancy, energization, or live-service record.
actions.evidence_note: Official KCMO Legistar/clerk record for Rocky Branch Creek data center campus.

actions.action_type: major MPD amendment / preliminary development plan and plat approval
actions.result_status: Council passed Committee Substitute Ordinance 240198 approving a major amendment to a Master Planned Development preliminary development plan, also serving as a preliminary plat, on about 500 acres at the northeast corner of I-435 and Highway 169 to allow six data centers and two office buildings.
actions.access_caveat: Preliminary development-plan/plat approval; current Port KC project page later describes five hyperscale data-center buildings.
actions.evidence_note: Official KCMO Legistar record; creates a scope conflict with the current Port KC project page on building count.

actions.result_status: The Board adopted a resolution authorizing up to $10 billion of Port KC taxable revenue bonds for Project Mica and related documents. The official minutes record unanimous approval.
actions.vote_tally: 6 yes / 0 no; Chairperson and five commissioners/councilpersons listed aye
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: Project Mica taxable revenue bonds; resolution number not exposed in reviewed minutes
actions.access_caveat: Financing authority is not a building permit, land-use approval, construction start, or energized service.
actions.evidence_note: Official Port KC minutes; amount is maximum principal authorization.

actions.result_status: Port KC's current Project Mica page describes a nearly 500-acre Kansas City Northland development at the northeast corner of I-435 and Highway 169, including five hyperscale data-center buildings totaling 1.56 million square feet and a full-development draw of nearly 700 MW supplied by the adjacent Nashua Power Station and onsite substations.
actions.access_caveat: Official project-page scope; not a building permit, energization, commissioning, or live-service record.
actions.evidence_note: Used as current capacity and physical-scope source.

actions.result_status: Google confirmed Project Mica and its Kansas City Northland context; the report describes a 500-acre, $10 billion development and Google energy-cost responsibility.
actions.access_caveat: Local report; no government permit or independent construction record is inferred.
actions.evidence_note: Tier-4 company-confirmation report, kept separate from Port KC financing.

actions.result_status: Trade reporting stated construction began at Google's second Kansas City campus. No building permit, inspection, or utility record was located to independently verify the start.
actions.access_caveat: Specialist trade report based on project information; not a government construction record.
actions.evidence_note: Construction claim explicitly labeled as trade/company evidence.

actions.result_status: KSHB reported Google confirmed construction underway for a second Kansas City data-center campus, published photos/captions of cranes building Project Mica at the northeast corner of I-435 and US-169, and quoted Google and Evergy on the capacity-commitment energy-cost framework.
actions.access_caveat: Local media and company statements; no permit, inspection, energization, commissioning, or service record is inferred.
actions.evidence_note: Supports status layer of site work-construction when paired with official local approvals.

actions.result_status: Google's current data-center location material lists Kansas City, Missouri as in development; it does not provide a building, permit, energization, or service date.
actions.access_caveat: Company status page; current listing is not a local approval or live-service record.

capacity_mw_note: Port KC describes the full development as drawing nearly 700 MW; rounded to 700 MW for structured capacity. This is utility draw / power requirement, not confirmed IT load or energized capacity.

history.previous_value: Port KC authorized up to $10 billion in Project Mica taxable revenue bonds on 2025-07-28 by unanimous vote. Google and trade reporting later identified active development/construction, and Google's current location material lists Kansas City, Missouri in development. No building-level permit, inspection, CO, utility interconnection, energization, commissioning, or live-service record was located. Bond authorization is not treated as construction approval.
history.reason: Refreshed with official KCMO development-plan approvals, current Port KC project scope, Google location listing, and local/trade construction-underway reporting.
Port KC current project page says full development will draw nearly 700 MW.
Google official locations page lists Kansas City, Missouri in development; local/trade reports identify Project Mica as Google's campus.

sources.match_reason: Exact Phase3↔regional stable-ID pair; seed merged only with explicit evidence

contradictions.details: KCMO Ordinance 240198 approved a roughly 500-acre preliminary development plan/plat allowing six data centers and two office buildings, while Port KC's current Project Mica page describes five hyperscale data-center buildings totaling 1.56 million square feet. Structured scope follows the newer official Port KC project page; the older KCMO entitlement remains in actions.
